# Quantum Chirality Receiver

> One ordered product triple of qubits, one label per triple, and an unknown common proper orientation. A calibrated unital qubit memory is useful across the first gap exactly when its Bloch matrix has Frobenius norm greater than one.

For volume magnitude d and a known unital first-gap memory with Bloch matrix T, the exact finite minimax success is 1/2 + (d/12) max(1, ||T||_F). The lower bound is pointwise in the source orientation. The upper bound allows arbitrary classical side records and unlimited later coherent storage. The attaining receiver uses two possible Bell settings on the first pair and single-qubit feed-forward on the final specimen, with only classical storage across the second gap. A nonunital amplitude-damping example gives a separate achievable gain from an early partial measurement.

## Scientific account

- [Orientation and theorem](science/model.md) defines the ordered product input, shared unknown frame, and allowed memory.
- [Exact converse](science/converse.md) gives the rotation average, early classical-storage bound, and arbitrary-instrument proof for unital memory.
- [Staged receiver](science/receiver.md) gives the weighted Bell measurement, readout, and physical timing.
- [Channel examples and nonunital extension](science/memory-channels.md) separates the exact unital theorem from the amplitude-damping lower bound.
- [Attribution](references/RELATED_WORK.md) compares the result with established chirality, joint measurement, and noisy-storage work.
